name: Joseph of Arimathea

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Joseph of Arimathea was a merchant and an Arthurian hero. He appears only briefly in the Christian Bible. He plays a large role in the story of the Grail. At his house, on the night before his death, Jesus held the Last Supper, where the Grail served as part of the meal. The object, a chalice or a platter, was sanctified by transubstantiation. Joseph buried Jesus after the crucifixion on Mount Golgotha. He was the only disciple, and perhaps an uncle, rich enough to pay for the tomb. For this service the Roman official Pontius Pilate gave him the Grail. Joseph then traveled the Mediterranean, bearing the Grail and converting people to the new religion. He finally settled in Britain, a land he once visited with Jesus as a boy. He passed up the tin mines of Cornwall to live in Glastonbury. On Wearyall Hill he thrust his staff into the ground, and it burst into bloom in winter. He built the first Christian church in Britain there.
objective: Document Joseph of Arimathea and his role in the Grail story.
